1.1.3.3-r1.burton_quote: than the Body is well able to bear, it must needs be distempered, saith Faventinus, & diseased

1.1.3.3-r2.burton_quote: Faventinus, a cause of dotage, & produceth milder symptoms: if hot, they are rash, raving mad, or inclining to it

1.1.3.3-r3.burton_quote: Hippocrates in his book of Melancholy (if at least it be his) giving instance in a burning coal, which when it is hot, shines; when it is cold, looks black, and so doth the humour
